method_notes.xgboost_calibrated: Gradient-boosted trees on 16 causal features, isotonic-calibrated on validation.
method_notes.zscore_max: Statistical baseline: max |z| vs healthy training data; threshold tuned on validation.
method_notes.alarm_threshold_rule: Conventional alarm: winding ≥ 130 °C or vibration ≥ 4.5 mm/s (no tuning).
method_notes.temperature_extrapolation: Heuristic: linear 30-min temperature trend reaches 155 °C within the horizon.

detection.notes: Fault onset is the scripted initiation time; many faults are physically invisible for some time after onset, so detection delay includes the latent period.

diagnosis.notes: Rows labelled with a fault right after onset are often not yet observable.

latency.scope: 3 calibrated horizons + isolation forest + diagnosis for one feature row, CPU

policy_notes.rule_derate: Alarm (≥130 °C or ≥4.5 mm/s) → reduce load 30 %; ≥145 °C or ≥6.5 mm/s → shutdown.
policy_notes.rule_shutdown_on_alarm: Alarm → controlled shutdown (stays down; fault left for later repair).
policy_notes.foresight_estimated: Risk-triggered agent (deterministic planner) → Future Branching from the telemetry-estimated state → verifier → auto-approved action.
policy_notes.foresight_oracle: Same loop, but branches simulate the hidden true state (upper bound).

interventions.approval_note: Recommended actions were auto-approved by the harness (simulation only).

deterministic.source: agent runs triggered inside the closed-loop intervention evaluation

live.verifier_label: v2 (before the vibration-margin and strict-improvement fixes)

live_recheck.verifier_label: v3 (vibration margin, strict improvement, horizon; v4 not yet re-checked)

limitations: All data is synthetic, produced by the project's own digital twin; the twin's physics and fault models are simplified (lumped thermal node, parametric bearing damage growth).
The predictive models are trained and tested on the same simulator family, so test results measure generalisation across randomized episodes, not transfer to real machines.
Intervention outcomes depend on illustrative economic parameters (simulation/params.py).
In the closed-loop evaluation, approvals are auto-granted by the harness; the live system requires explicit human approval.

The closed-loop agent is the deterministic planner; live model runs (Meta Model API and Fireworks AI) are reported separately as single-decision snapshots, not closed-loop episodes. The planner, the verifier, and the regret audit share the same simulator.
Sample sizes are small (a handful of episodes per scenario), so confidence intervals are wide.
